finding: src/anomaly/review.py:655 F5 is not fully resolved: `_markdown_text` escapes Markdown delimiters but leaves dataset-controlled bare `http://`/`https://` URLs, which GitHub-Flavored Markdown recognizes as extended autolinks. Neutralize URL schemes as well as link/HTML delimiters, and revise the test to detect rendered/scan-visible links rather than only checking that the original raw syntax disappeared.
rationale: The production detector interpolates dataset-derived candidate_id values into statements, the report path passes those statements through _markdown_text, and that function demonstrably preserves bare HTTPS URLs that GFM renders as links while the current test asserts only that the original inline-link and HTML-tag strings disappeared.

evidence.output: detect.py reads candidate_id from each query result and builds statement = f"{category} lead for {candidate_id}"; draft_findings preserves signal.statement, accept_findings promotes it, and write_report serializes it with _markdown_text. _markdown_text collapses whitespace, HTML-escapes, and backslash-escapes Markdown delimiters but has no URL-scheme guard.
'Acme \\[click\\]\\(https://example.invalid/pixel\\) <img src=https://example.invalid/pixel> \\#\\# Forged heading' — both bare HTTPS URLs remain.

evidence.command: read GFM spec section 6.9, extended URL autolinks, lines 10989-11038
evidence.output: The spec states that http:// or https:// followed by a valid domain is recognized as an extended URL autolink and shows the rendered HTML as <a href="...">.

The inertness test checks only that the original [click](https://...) string, raw string, and newline heading are absent; it never asserts that outbound URLs or rendered/scan-visible links are absent.
